title: A · A joke in three shots
lesson: Tell a joke in three shots, setup, twist, punchline, then design your end card. Every shot is your decision: you brief it, compare takes, choose.

frames.task: Design the presenter: two or three candidates from a short description, or a photo the designer brings. They pick.

slots.task: Set up the joke: the situation everyone in the room recognises. Brief it with the shot card, draft it twice on veo-fast changing ONE thing (light or distance), compare the two takes, choose, then render the final on veo.

slots.purpose: Twist: the detail that turns it, no face
slots.task: Your first render. The twist: the one detail that turns the situation, shown without a face. Brief it with three fields: what the viewer should get, the one action, the sound.

slots.purpose: Punchline: your presenter says it in German
slots.task: The punchline. Design your presenter: ask for two or three start-frame candidates or bring a photo, and pick one. Write the German line yourself, 14 words at most: timing beats length. Render, then fix one thing.

Design your end card. Write the tag line, then the look: a solid colour, the last frame of your punchline frozen and blurred behind the text, or your own image; text colour, size, centred or low, your logo. Ask for a still preview, it is instant and free, and iterate until you like it.
slots.purpose: End card: your tag line and your look

note: The prompts in prompts/ are worked examples and the source of the reserve clips, not the starting point: the designer briefs each slot from its task.
